 DELL Price Target — 24/7 Wall St. Dell has grown well beyond its PC beginnings. AI-optimized servers brought in $16.40 billion last quarter, and the AI backlog ended the quarter at a record $95 billion. 
 A 306% Rally Meets a Volatile October 
 Dell shares are up 306.45% year to date and 11.31% over the past week, including an 8.38% gain today. The stock is still down 9.94% over the past month and sits about 14.9% below its 52-week high of $594.69. 
 In fiscal Q2, reported September 1, revenue rose 57.8% to $46.97 billion, beating the $44.44 billion estimate. Non-GAAP EPS came in at $7.04, well above the $4.90 consensus. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $192 billion and now expects non-GAAP EPS of $25.50.

 DELL Price Scenario — 24/7 Wall St. Why Bulls See $627 Ahead 
 The bull case reaches $627.66. Dell booked $60.9 billion in AI orders last quarter and now has more than 6,500 AI customers. Management expects $74 billion in AI server revenue this fiscal year, and the expansion goes well beyond the chipmakers (we highlighted seven of the power, cooling, and networking names riding the same wave in a free report here). 
 Traditional servers grew 122%, and ISG operating margin expanded to 15% from 8.8%. Analysts have a consensus target of $593, with 20 Buy or Strong Buy ratings and no Sells. Price targets from individual firms were not available. 
 Story Continues DELL Analyst Ratings — 24/7 Wall St. Cash Flow and Supply Limits Are the Risks to Watch 
 The bear case falls to $427.71. Free cash flow fell 47.2% to $986 million, and shareholders' equity stands at -$1.43B. Management also noted shortages of DRAM, NAND and CPUs, and said rising component costs account for part of the growth in traditional servers. 
 There are offsets. Management reported adjusted free cash flow of $8.1 billion and a core leverage ratio of 0.8x. Negative equity also sits alongside large payouts to shareholders: a record $4.3B last quarter. 
 How Dell Compares to HPE and Super Micro 
 Hewlett Packard Enterprise ( NYSE:HPE ) is Dell's closest rival in servers and storage. HPE's non-GAAP operating margin of 16.2% beats Dell's 12.6%. But HPE only expects 13%-17% revenue growth next fiscal year, which helps explain why Dell trades at a premium. 
 Super Micro Computer ( NASDAQ:SMCI ) is the pure-play AI server peer. It trades at 9 times earnings, compared with 25 for Dell. Super Micro also used $6.8 billion in operating cash in fiscal 2026 and faces a board review related to export controls. Against this peer group, our target looks reasonable.

 Dell Earns a Buy Rating at $506 
 The 24/7 Wall St. price target of $568.76 has a buy rating and 90% confidence. The backlog is the deciding factor. 
 Dell trades at about 19 times forward earnings. Bullish prospects strengthen if AI orders keep turning into revenue as supply eases. Bearish risks grow if free cash flow keeps falling further behind earnings. Right now, the evidence favors the bulls.
